# The improvement campaign as an operating system — map, audit, and five changes

Read-only pass over `/Users/mihaiperdum/Projects/goose/evals/swarm-bench/nodeloop/`. Nothing was executed against the fleet, nothing written. Numbers below are read off source and off the result rows on disk.

---

## 1. What the machine is

| layer | file | role |
|---|---|---|
| control surface | `/Users/mihaiperdum/Projects/goose/evals/swarm-bench/nodeloop/loop.sh` | `start / status / check / preflight / boundary / abort / stop / results / selftest` |
| supervisor | `.../nodeloop/sweep.py` (1711 lines) | ARMS × QUESTIONS × reps → `backlog()` → `run_unit()` → `nodeloop-result.json` |
| entrant driver | `.../bench/run_build.py` | spawns `target/release/goose swarm run`, then `score_build.gather/evaluate` |
| grader | `.../bench/score_build.py` | 35 checks, tiers A .25 / B .30 / C .25 / D .20 |
| doctrine | `GOAL.md`, `PREREGISTERED.md`, `PREDICTIONS`, `MARKERS`, `RESUME.md`, `FINDINGS.md` (1.08 MB), `GOALS.jsonl` |

**sweep.py mechanics that matter**

- `ARMS` (line 93) = one lever per arm, each carrying a written gate. `QUESTIONS` (line 489) = the *scheduled* cells; `cells()` (656) joins them and **warns loudly in both directions** — a question naming a missing arm is skipped, an arm with `reps>0` named in no question is reported as an orphan (this exact hole silently killed `scoped_contracts`, F170).
- `reps` is per-cell: **mechanism readouts are `reps: 1`, score comparisons `reps: 3`**, with `MIN_REPS = 5` and `CURVE_REPS = 8` (F327: the sign test's bar is a sawtooth in n; 6 and 7 pairs are a *harder* test than 5).
- `complete()` (713) is the anti-contamination gate: a unit counts as done only if `audit_version` **and** `engine_build` match current, and it is not `abandoned` / `aborted` / node-short. `engine_build()` = mtime+size of `target/release/goose`.
- **VOID** = `actual_nodes != nodes` from `run_started.pool` (1244). The label is intention, the pool event is fact.
- `is_real_unit()` (811) is the F349 patch: `harness_ok is False` → not real, **and** an independent `wall_secs < 60` floor, deliberately two conditions because "a gate that shares its only input with the thing it guards goes silent when that input is missing".
- `QUEUE` (58, `arms_now()` 1286) lets an arm be added to a *running* supervisor — but appended, so it lands last. No `QUEUE` file exists right now.
- `backlog()` (1385) + `curve_first()` (1309) order the work; `curve_first` is a **pure function of what is still incomplete**, with a self-test (`curve_order_self_test`, 1330) that requires the *old* `zip_longest` rule to FAIL the same simulation.

**loop.sh mechanics that matter**

- `start` **parks** the previous run tree first (`cp -R "$RUNDIR" "$PARK"`, and counts source vs destination run logs — the earlier `/*/ ` form collapsed twelve unit dirs into one and destroyed the campaign's only 1-node log).
- `start` refuses to launch if `preflight` fails — an absent lever is byte-identical to baseline and records a *fabricated null*.
- `check` = `health.py` + held-commit counter (≥8 → "CROSS THE BOUNDARY", not advisory) + stale-supervisor detector (a running interpreter never sees a source edit).
- `boundary` = STOP → **supervisor before engine** (killing the engine first makes the sweep score a half-finished tree; measured, it wrote `score=0.2999, void=false` indistinguishable from a real row) → fleet must be idle → rebuild → wait for the artifact to settle → verify every `MARKERS` line with `grep -qF -- "$M" <(strings ...)` (no pipe; `pipefail` + grep's early exit made present markers read ABSENT) → reclaim `target/debug` → assert four evidence paths still exist.
- `preflight.py` answers the same question **from source, with nothing killed**, and distinguishes LITERAL / DERIVED (serde `rename_all` generates the literal at compile time) / COMMENT / ABSENT.

**Instruments — what each answers, from which events**

| instrument | question | source |
|---|---|---|
| `occupancy.py` (occ-5) | busy node-seconds / (wall × pool); biggest task's share; solo tail; idle-node mechanisms (judge / pre_review / speculated / replanned); `max_useful_nodes` | `task_dispatched`, `task_completed`, `judge_observed`→`judge_verdict`, `pre_review.secs`, `plan_loaded` |
| `failures.py` | **which KIND** of dispatch fails (implementer / test-author / verify-sink). Refuses to print a pooled rate; asserts physical bounds; classifies the sink by id before owned files | `task_dispatched.owned_files`, `task_completed.status` |
| `curve.py` (curve-1) | GOAL ONE's verdict: one-sided sign test over matched pairs, wall and score separately; enforces all four `PREREGISTERED.md` falsifiers; prints the replan-bonus confound beside the verdict | stored `nodeloop-result.json` + `bonusclass` over `run.jsonl` |
| `power.py` | *can the design reach the bar at all?* q = P(a random n3 cell outscores a random n1 cell); `q_for_power`/`gap_for_q` | the n3 cells' own sd |
| `planshape.py` | what the redraft ladder **buys** — accepted vs discarded plan, width/depth/roots/test-task shape | `retarget_discarded.tasks[]` vs `plan_loaded.tasks[]` (different key names for the same field) |
| `review.py` (rev-1) | the tick review, four levels in Mihai's order: LOGS → PLAN → GOAL → OVERARCHING; settles `PREDICTIONS` by `strings`-matching the running binary, and refuses to attribute a binary newer than the run | run `*.jsonl` + `PREDICTIONS` + `GOAL.md` + the binary |
| `goalstate.py` | the **stall detector**: ≥10 ticks with no metric move ⇒ demand a shake-up. Streak keyed on the *measured* `failures.py` row, not on the goal string; absent flags carry forward (F290) | `GOALS.jsonl` + `failures.py` over runs newer than `binary_mtime()` |
| `health.py` | "is the loop working or only alive" — heartbeat staleness, no-unit-in-4h, disk, consecutive fails. OK/WARN/BAD | loop log, result rows, `sweep.engine_build()` |
| `dispatch_audit.py` (da-3) | grades the **instructions**, not the artifact: kind mismatch, specificity, blind spots (runtime-created tasks whose instruction is not in the log at all), context slices, fleet collapse | `task_dispatched`, `rules_delivered`, `levers_resolved`, `plan_loaded` |
| `promptbench.py` | the seconds-scale offline loop: replay archived worker decision points; does the model ACT or TALK | `~/.local/state/goose/logs/llm_request.*.jsonl` |
| `reaudit.py` | recompute the audit **from stored logs, in place** — so an instrument fix ships mid-campaign instead of costing 2 h/unit of re-runs | stored `run.jsonl` |

## 2. What this operating system does genuinely well

1. **Falsification is mechanised, not remembered.** `curve.py`'s four falsifiers are asserted in `self_test()` *in both directions* — including the one most likely to be rationalised later ("wall-clock without score is a FAIL, not a partial win"). `controls.py` tests the grader HIGH/LOW/**ISOLATION**. `curve_order_self_test` requires the previous implementation to fail. That is a real discipline: a test the old code also passes proves nothing.
2. **Predictions are registered where a machine can settle them**, with the build-attribution problem solved. `PREDICTIONS` pairs each claim with a **string literal that must be in the running binary**, and `review.py:236-273` marks a prediction NOT-SETTLEABLE rather than failed when the literal is absent — the "uncontrolled zero" rule applied to the operator's own claims. `F350`/`F351` added struct fields and no literal, so they take `judge_node` (09:06) as a *declared* build-boundary proxy instead of a silent conflation.
3. **Instruments are reused, never re-implemented (L2).** `curve.py` imports `bonusclass`, `review.py` imports `occupancy` (with a note that a local re-derivation gave the wrong answer), `goalstate.py` imports `failures`, `promptbench.py` imports `failures`' classifier, `F385` extended `power.py`'s own functions rather than re-deriving them.
4. **Provenance is enforced at the only place that matters.** `complete()` re-runs anything not on the current engine+audit; `curve.py` falsifier 2 drops a pair spanning a rebuild; `reaudit.py` exists so an instrument bump does not cost fleet time.
5. **The harness audits itself every unit.** `selftest.py` runs per unit (up to 600 s) and its verdict is written to `harness_ok` — and the finding that it *was computed and then dropped at the return statement* is recorded in the code (1276-1280).
6. **Retractions are first-class.** RESUME.md carries a "what today disproved" table listing four of the author's own headlines as DEAD. `F385` publishes catching itself reaching for `pstdev` because it made the design look 27% more feasible (L225). This is the rarest property in the whole system and it is the reason the numbers here are worth anything.
7. **Bands were converted to identities where variance made bands unsettleable** (L224: F357 became a within-run identity, F386 a within-row identity). That is exactly the right move on a fleet with a 46-point replicate spread.

## 3. Where it is weak or mis-aimed

### W1 — The registered objective is the *wrong* objective under the reframe, and it actively penalises the desired outcome
`PREREGISTERED.md` falsifier 3 and `curve.py:verdict()`: *"wall-clock favouring 3 nodes WITHOUT score doing the same is a FAIL"*, and `both = p_wall < 0.05 and p_score < 0.05`. Under the reframe, wall clock is a **constraint**, not a co-objective. A swarm that is 1.4× slower and +0.10 better — the literal thing being asked for — is scored by this instrument as **NOT SUPPORTED**. Worse, `verdict()` has no cost axis at all: nothing anywhere computes score per node-second, score per joule, or score at equal compute. `occupancy.py` emits `busy_node_secs` and `loop.sh results` prints score / spread / fallbacks / kind-mm% / wall — **the two halves of "quality per node-second" are never divided by each other in any file in the tree.**

### W2 — There is no interaction cell, so the reframe's actual question is not in the design
Every entry in `QUESTIONS` except the node curve is `"nodes": 3`. The node curve is `baseline` only. So the design can measure *lever effect at 3 nodes* or *node effect with no lever*, and **never** `Δquality(lever) at n3 − Δquality(lever) at n1` — which is the only quantity that says "this mechanism converts spare hardware into quality". Given F405 (arms identical on the 24 reproducible checks), the main effect is known to be ≈0; continuing to spend the queue on it while the interaction is unmeasurable is the central mis-aim.

### W3 — The measured "quality" is dominated by scorer non-reproducibility, and the campaign pays for that in fleet hours instead of removing it for free
F402: re-running the **same binaries** against a fresh vendor and clean DB makes `sync_shape` succeed in the two cells the scorer recorded as broken. F405: the entire +0.0593 lives in the 11 non-reproducing checks; on the stable 24 the arms are 0.8097 vs 0.8089. Yet each unit is scored **exactly once**, at a cost of ~2 h of fleet, while a second scoring pass over the stored tree costs seconds. Every number in `power.py` and F385's 51/115-pair table is computed from an sd that includes scorer noise the campaign has already proven is removable. **A significant part of "51 pairs" is self-inflicted.**

### W4 — The partition that produced the campaign's most important finding exists only in prose
`grep -rn "STABLE\|stable_24" nodeloop/*.py bench/*.py` returns **nothing**. F409 pre-registers the 24-check stable set in `PREDICTIONS`; `curve.py`, `power.py` and `summarise()` all still operate on the pooled 35-check score. The next verdict this system publishes will therefore be computed on the metric F405 showed to be noise.

### W5 — The corpus is structurally uncollectable under the campaign's own tick rules, and this has already happened
`complete()` invalidates every row on a rebuild. GOAL.md rule 3b makes `loop.sh check` demand a boundary at 8 held commits, "and that is not advisory". RESUME.md records **five rebuilds on 2026-08-05 alone** (13:17, 15:07, 15:58, 16:32, 16:42, 17:25). An observation costs ~2 h. The arithmetic is closed: a design needing 8 pairs (`CURVE_REPS`), let alone 51 (F385), cannot survive a boundary policy that fires several times a day.

**Read off the rows on disk right now** (`/Users/mihaiperdum/Projects/goose/evals/swarm-bench/runs/nodeloop/*/nodeloop-result.json`):

| cell | score | wall | engine_build | harness_ok |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `baseline-n3-r0` | 0.3895 | 10195.3 | **1785939939-235858816** | true |
| `baseline-n3-r1` | 0.4780 | 8488.0 | 1785868965-235742608 | true |
| `baseline-n3-r2` | 0.6030 | 6752.6 | 1785868965-235742608 | true |
| `baseline-n3-r3` | 0.8157 | 7302.6 | 1785868965-235742608 | true |
| `baseline-n1-r0` | 0.5798 | 5842.9 | 1785868965-235742608 | true |
| `baseline-n1-r1..r7`, `n2-r0..r10`, and every treatment arm | 0.0 | **0.1-0.2 s** | 1785868965 | **false** |

Applying `pair_up()`'s rules by hand: rep 0 is dropped by falsifier 2 (**different engine builds**); reps 1-3 are dropped because their n1 half is a 0.1-second non-run; reps 4-7 are dropped on both halves. **The campaign currently holds ZERO valid matched pairs**, and its single real n1 observation is on a build no surviving n3 cell shares. Also: **no treatment arm has ever produced a real score row** — `doc_fetch-n3-r0`, the arm F390/F405 name as the only one that matters, is a 0.1 s fabrication.

### W6 — The target of the reframe is not on the board
`bench/run_build.py:28` already defines `MODELS = {"opus-5": ..., "sonnet-5": ..., "haiku-4.5": ...}` and an `aws_bedrock` invocation path. `sweep.py` only ever builds `entrant = f"swarm-{nodes}node"`. So the ~0.95 strong-model anchor and the ~0.84 single-local-agent anchor — the two endpoints of the gap the whole project exists to close — **are measurable with existing code and are scheduled nowhere.** No artefact in the repo records them; progress toward "strong-model quality" is currently unfalsifiable.

### W7 — Registration has drifted into three incompatible n's
`PREREGISTERED.md` (frozen, "nothing below may be edited after a pair lands; a change goes in as a dated amendment") says **5 pairs**. `sweep.py:CURVE_REPS` says **8** (justified only in a code comment, F327). F385 says **51**. `PREREGISTERED.md` was last modified 2026-08-04 22:33 and contains **no amendment**. The registration document is no longer the operating design, which quietly costs the pre-registration its power.

### W8 — Two guards are stale in ways that read as green
- **`loop.sh results` / `sweep.summarise()` print `n = len(rs)` (every row) while the mean is computed from the filtered `ok` list.** So the operator-facing table reports `baseline / 1 node / n=8` with a mean drawn from **one** cell. The filter is correct; the column beside it is not.
- **`goalstate.py`'s streak is keyed on a metric that can no longer move.** It keys on the `failures.py` test-author row; F252 closed that row (11 completions, 0 failures) and both levers are default ON. `GOALS.jsonl`'s last tick is **2026-08-05 07:34**, ~14 h before F408 landed at 22:03 — the one guard designed to survive context compaction has not been ticked through the entire day it was most needed, and its metric is now structurally frozen.

### W9 — Population n = 1, and the campaign's own G7 warns about exactly this
One spec (`spec-build.md`, 3930 bytes), one app shape (`vendorsync`), one language, 35 checks, `TIER_WEIGHT` fixed. F125/F126 are honest about it ("a pattern in one population is a hypothesis until a second sees it"), and G7 indicts the engine for being 5-10× more Python-aware than anything else — but **the bench is Python-shaped too**, so the overfit G7 warns about is invisible to every instrument here.

### W10 — Queue head-of-line blocking, formalised
`backlog()` hoists baseline, then `curve_first()` hoists the n3/n1 curve to the front, and `CURVE_REPS = 8` means **16 baseline cells (~32 h)** stand ahead of every treatment arm — to estimate an effect F405 already measured at +0.0007. Meanwhile the mechanism arms are `reps: 1`, so the levers that spend spare nodes on checking (`sink_review`, `spec_repair`, `complete_parallel`, `owned_file_fence`) can only ever answer "did it fire", never "did it help".

## 4. Five concrete changes to the CAMPAIGN

### C1 — Replace the verdict function: quality is the objective, wall-clock is a constraint
File a **dated amendment** in `PREREGISTERED.md` (the document's own rule) retiring falsifier 3, and change `curve.py:verdict()` accordingly:
- primary readout: `score_stable` (C2/C3) on the pre-registered 24;
- secondary readout: `quality_per_node_second = score_stable / busy_node_secs`, taking `busy_node_secs` from `occupancy.py`'s existing JSON (L2 — do not re-derive);
- wall-clock demoted to a **gate**: `n3_wall <= K * n1_wall` (K registered before the next pair), reported as PASS/FAIL beside the verdict, never as a co-objective.
Add both columns to `loop.sh results` / `summarise()`, and fix the `n` column to print `len(ok)` with dropped rows shown separately. Without this, the instrument that publishes the verdict scores the reframe's success condition as a failure.

### C2 — Make scoring a repeated measure over the stored tree, before buying a single extra pair
Add `rescore.py` next to `reaudit.py` and on the same principle (*recompute from stored evidence, never re-run the fleet*): re-run `score_build.gather/evaluate` **k=5 times against the stored tree**, each with a fresh vendor mock and clean DB, and record a per-check **pass rate** instead of a single 0/1. Then:
- `score_stable` = mean pass-rate over the 24 stable checks; `score_flaky` reported separately, never averaged in;
- feed the *reduced* sd into `power.py` and re-publish the pairs-required table.
This attacks F402/F405 at the root: the noise that made 51 pairs necessary is measurement noise, and it costs seconds to remove where a pair costs 4 h. It also turns F409's stable set from a post-hoc judgement into an **empirically derived** one (a check whose rate is neither 0 nor 1 across k rescorings of the same tree is by definition non-reproducing). Controls both ways, as this campaign already demands: assert that a deliberately broken tree still scores low across all k.

### C3 — Put the stable set and both anchors into the instruments
- Freeze `STABLE_CHECKS` as a constant (sourced from `PREDICTIONS` F409) imported by `curve.py`, `power.py` and `summarise()`, with a self-test that fails if the set silently changes size — a partition that lives in prose is not a partition.
- Schedule two **reference cells** that are not fleet units in the usual sense: `anchor-opus` (existing `run_build` bedrock path, `MODELS["opus-5"]`) and `anchor-solo` (one local agent, no swarm), re-measured **once per epoch** and printed as two fixed columns on every results table. The claim under test becomes *"the swarm closes X% of the anchor gap per node-second"*, which is the reframe stated as a number. Today that gap exists only in the operator's head.

### C4 — Redesign the arm grid around the interaction, not the main effect
Change `QUESTIONS` so that every lever whose *mechanism is redundancy* — `sink_review`, `spec_repair`, `complete_parallel`, `owned_file_fence`, plus judge/pre-review as ON/OFF rather than only `prereview_off` — is scheduled as a **paired cell at n3 and n1** with `reps >= 3`, and register the readout as the difference-in-differences `Δscore_stable(lever)|n3 − Δscore_stable(lever)|n1`. Rationale, stated before running: F405 puts the main effect at +0.0007, so the main-effect design is spending 32 h to re-measure a zero; the interaction is the only place a "spare hardware becomes quality" effect can appear, and difference-in-differences cancels the level differences (replan bonus, barrier structure) that `bonusclass.py` and F406 show contaminate the direct comparison. Correspondingly, **retire the `reps: 1` rule for redundancy levers only** — "did it fire" is settled for these; "did it help" is the open question — and keep `reps: 1` for genuine mechanism probes.

### C5 — Freeze a measurement EPOCH, and move engine iteration to the seconds-scale loop
The corpus cannot be collected while the binary changes hourly (W5: zero valid pairs on disk right now, one of them lost purely to a mid-curve rebuild). Concretely:
- stamp each row with an `epoch_id` and pin `engine_build` for the epoch; `loop.sh check` should **refuse the boundary while the open epoch is below its registered pair count**, in the same spirit as `start` refusing without preflight — the held-commit counter currently argues only one way;
- between epochs, engine work is validated on `promptbench.py` (seconds per sample) and `rescore.py` (seconds per artefact), which is Lesson 78's own conclusion and is currently the loop the campaign owns but does not schedule;
- pair the freeze with a queue cap so `CURVE_REPS` cannot hold 16 baseline cells at the head of the queue — schedule the epoch as *k pairs of the decisive arm* rather than *8 pairs of baseline*, so an epoch produces an attributable result before the next boundary arrives.
- housekeeping in the same pass: quarantine the ~100 fabricated 0.1 s rows out of `runs/nodeloop/` (they are already filtered by `is_real_unit`, but they inflate the `n` column and every future glob), and re-key `goalstate.py`'s streak onto `score_stable` / `quality_per_node_second` so the stall detector watches a metric that can still move.

---

## 5. One-line verdict for the next operator

The falsification discipline here is better than most research code and should not be touched; what is broken is the **objective function and the schedule**. The campaign is spending its fleet proving a main effect it has already measured at +0.0007, on a metric it has already proven does not reproduce, under a rebuild policy that destroys the corpus before any registered n can be reached — while the two anchors that define the actual goal (strong model ≈0.95, solo local ≈0.84) are one scheduling line away in `run_build.py` and appear nowhere on the board.
